text:
maria: Quick check — internal control-plane (routing / quotas / telemetry) design. Do we standardize on REST/JSON or gRPC/protobufs for the service-to-service layer + gateway patterns? Thinking about console UX and rollout complexity.

kevin: +1 grpc between services. compact payloads, proto contracts make telemetry typing easier.

sasha: grpc is nice but the console is a web client — we'll need grpc-web or a gateway translation layer. extra infra and complexity :thinking_face: 

ben: hybrid approach sounds pragmatic: grpc for S2S, gateway exposes REST for console. keep strong typing internally, easy for third-party and console. Also preserve route headers like `X-Tenant-ID` for routing.

carla: quota enforcement is simplest at the gateway if it's JSON-based, but we can push quota checks into runtime if we include proto metadata. tradeoffs on where to enforce.

sam_ops: Operational concern: rollout UX. Contract changes for proto are trickier to roll out across many services. whats the canary plan if we switch? :eyes:

kevin: Proto helps with non-breaking additions (new optional fields, field numbers). But schema drift across services still bites. Need versioning policy.

sasha: Telemetry angle: console needs per-route, token-level cost & latency. That favors stable route identifiers and metadata propagation (not opaque path rewrites). If gateway rewrites, tracing gets messy. Make sure `traceparent` and route labels survive translation.

maria: Important: routing policy decisions are policy-first (latency/cost/region). Gateway must preserve decision labels so console can display routing reasons.

ben: What about an edge adapter pattern? Edge translates REST->gRPC and injects routing labels. Keeps console simple and runtime typed.

carla: Edge adapter adds surface area and perf overhead. We should benchmark. propose an experiment: add grpc endpoint + edge adapter for a couple routes and measure.

sam_ops: I'll own the canary. Minimal plan: 10% traffic -> monitor latency, errors, telemetry fidelity. If metrics look good, increase.

dev-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for control-plane-v2 at 2025-03-14T12:04Z — 10% traffic

kevin: Suggest proto include top-level route metadata so both gateway and runtime can map it reliably. Example proto snippet: ```
message ControlReq {
  string route = 1;
  map<string, string> meta = 2;
  bytes payload = 3;
}
```

sasha: +1. Console should index on route id, not derived URL. Sam: can you ensure metrics mapping uses route id?

maria: Action items: Kevin draft proto with `route`/`meta`. Ben & Carla spin up edge-adapter POC. Sam create canary runbook and dashboard. Sync Thu 10am to review.

ben: :thumbsup: will post perf numbers and latency diff.

sam_ops: I'll add SLOs to the canary dashboard: p50/p95 latency, error rate, telemetry completeness (percent of requests with route label + trace).

carla: small note: include a fallback JSON path for 3rd-party integrations so we don't break external consumers.

maria: Thanks all. Closing for now — followups in RFC PR.
